objectives: Plan a weekly production schedule that keeps acids, alkalis and disinfectants apart
Calculate output and packaging needs for larger batches
Decide which equipment to buy first as volume grows
Organise a cooperative for bulk buying and shared production using the cooperative principles

blocks.text: Growth in cleaning products usually comes from one or two institutional customers who order every week. When that happens, 20 kg batches stop being enough. Scaling up is not just using a bigger drum: you need a schedule, larger equipment that is still safe to handle, more raw materials on hand, and often more hands. Many women find it easier to grow together, sharing bulk purchases and a workshop.

blocks.name: woman-factory
blocks.caption: A small production unit runs on a written weekly plan.

blocks.text: Equipment as you grow

head: Stage
Batch size
Key equipment
rows: Kitchen scale (1 g), 50 L plastic drums, long paddles, funnels
Platform scale (to about 150 kg), 120 to 200 L HDPE drums with bottom taps, drum stand
Mixing tank with an electric stirrer, filling machine, sealed storage tanks

blocks.text: A tap at the bottom of a raised drum is the most useful upgrade: you fill bottles by gravity instead of lifting and pouring heavy buckets, which reduces spills and back injuries. An electric stirrer must be suitable for wet areas and plugged into a properly earthed socket away from the drum.
A weekly schedule that keeps chemistry apart

Plan your week so that acid products, alkaline products and disinfectants are made on different days or in different drums, with drums washed and rinsed between products. This avoids contamination, such as LAS left in a drum turning your BKC cleaner cloudy, and it keeps the most hazardous steps away from busy filling days.

blocks.title: Sample production week
items: Mon: laundry, 100 kg
Tue: dish liquid, 100 kg
Wed: test, release, fill
Thu: floor and toilet gel
Fri: label, deliver, restock
blocks.caption: Separate days for different chemistry, with testing before filling.

blocks.title: Worked example: packaging for a 100 kg dish batch
blocks.context: For example, Funke wins a supply contract and moves her dish liquid to 100 kg batches, still in 500 ml bottles at 515 g each.
steps: Ingredients scale by 4 from her 25 kg sheet: LABSA 1.50 x 4 = 6.0 kg; SLES 2.00 x 4 = 8.0 kg; caustic finished by pH, starting from about 0.18 x 4 = 0.72 kg calculated.
Salt solution: she starts at her recorded 500 g per 25 kg, so 2.0 kg of 25% solution for 100 kg, then continues in small steps while timing the flow.
Bottles: 100,000 / 515 = 194.2, so 194 bottles.
Leftover: 100,000 minus (194 x 515) = 100,000 minus 99,910 = 90 g, which becomes her retained sample.
She orders 200 bottles, caps and labels per batch to allow for a few damaged ones.
blocks.result: Funke's purchase list, labour plan and filling time are all set before she mixes, and her four-times recipe is checked against the same test card as before.

blocks.text: Growing as a cooperative

A **cooperative**, as defined by the International Cooperative Alliance, is an autonomous association of people united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social and cultural needs through a jointly owned and democratically controlled enterprise. Its seven principles are: voluntary and open membership; democratic member control (one member, one vote in a primary cooperative); member economic participation; autonomy and independence; education, training and information; cooperation among cooperatives; and concern for community.

blocks.title: Worked example: bulk buying LABSA together
blocks.context: For example, five women in a Lagos market group each use about 8 kg of LABSA a month. A supplier offers a lower price for larger orders: suppose about ₦2,700 per kg for 40 kg instead of about ₦3,000 per kg for small amounts (illustrative figures only).
steps: Combined monthly need: 5 x 8 = 40 kg.
Saving per kg: 3,000 minus 2,700 = ₦300.
Total monthly saving: 40 x 300 = ₦12,000, which is ₦2,400 per member.
They agree in writing who receives the delivery, how it is weighed out into labelled containers, and that each member pays her share before the order is placed.
They keep the COA and one shared raw-material register, so every member's batches trace to the same lot.
blocks.result: Each member saves money every month, and the group builds a record of trust and paperwork that supports later steps such as a shared workshop or joint registration.

blocks.title: Registering the group
blocks.text: Cooperative societies in Nigeria are registered through the cooperative department of the state government. A business name or company is registered with the CAC. Visit your state cooperative office for current requirements before collecting any money from members, and keep written accounts that every member can see.

blocks.title: Bigger batches, bigger risks
blocks.text: At 100 kg, a caustic or LABSA splash involves more chemical and more heat. Keep the same order of addition, add caustic in more portions with longer waits, never lift drums alone, and train every member in PPE and first aid before she works in the room.

takeaways: Scale with a schedule, not just a bigger drum
Separate acid, alkaline and disinfectant production by day or drum
Calculate units, packaging and retained sample before each large batch
Cooperatives follow seven principles, including one member, one vote

activity.title: Draft your scale-up plan
steps: Write a one-week production schedule for at least three products, separating acid, alkaline and disinfectant days.
Scale one formula to 100 kg and calculate units, packaging and leftover.
List the next two pieces of equipment you would buy and why.
If you are in a group, draft a one-page bulk-buying agreement covering payment, weighing out and records.
activity.evidence: Your weekly schedule, 100 kg calculation, equipment list and, if relevant, the group agreement.

quiz.q: Ten dish bottles average 516.1 g against a 515 g target, but one weighs 514 g. What should Funke do?
options: Release the batch because the average is above target
Top up the light bottle and re-check more bottles before release
quiz.explain: Every bottle must meet the label amount. Correct the light bottle and check that the filling problem is not wider.

quiz.q: A customer complains that her laundry detergent separated into layers. What should you do first?
options: Ask for the batch number and compare her bottle with your retained sample and batch record
Tell her she shook it wrong
quiz.explain: The retained sample and batch record show whether the fault came from production or from storage or use.

quiz.q: Which container is best for the citric acid toilet gel sold to homes?
options: An HDPE angled-neck bottle with a child-resistant cap
quiz.explain: HDPE resists the acid, the angled neck reaches under the rim, and the child-resistant cap protects children.

quiz.q: A batch costs ₦26,000 in total and fills 20 bottles. What is the cost per bottle?
Chiamaka's cost is ₦1,145 per bottle and her wholesale price is ₦1,700. What is her profit per bottle at wholesale?
Why should laundry detergent and BKC disinfectant be made on different days or in separate, washed drums?
options: Leftover anionic surfactant can make the BKC cleaner cloudy and weaken it
quiz.explain: Cross-contamination between anionic products and BKC ties up the disinfectant.

quiz.q: Under the ICA cooperative principles, how are votes usually shared in a primary cooperative?
options: By how much money each member put in
quiz.explain: Democratic member control means equal voting rights, one member, one vote, in primary cooperatives.

finalQuiz.q: Which dirt needs an acid product?
options: Limescale and urine scale in a toilet
finalQuiz.explain: Mineral scale dissolves in acid. Grease and food soil respond to alkaline or neutral surfactant products.

finalQuiz.q: Which pair must never be mixed?
options: Bleach and an acid toilet cleaner
finalQuiz.explain: Bleach with acid releases chlorine gas. Bleach with ammonia releases chloramine gases. Neither must ever happen.

finalQuiz.q: Hauwa's store has one shelf. What is the safest fix?
options: Create separate zones for acids, alkalis, bleach and flammables with gaps between them
Put bleach and citric acid together at the back
Store IPA beside the window in the sun
finalQuiz.explain: Separate zones stop leaks or mistakes from bringing incompatible chemicals together.

finalQuiz.q: How much caustic soda is calculated for 2.0 kg of 96% LABSA, using about 0.118 kg per kg?
finalQuiz.explain: 2.0 x 0.118 = 0.236 kg, about 0.24 kg. Add about 90% first and finish by pH.

finalQuiz.q: Why is soda ash added only after the LABSA is neutralised?
options: Added to raw acid it fizzes, releasing carbon dioxide
finalQuiz.explain: Soda ash reacts with the acid and fizzes. Neutralise with caustic first, then add soda ash as the builder.

finalQuiz.q: A 25 kg dish batch has a density of 1.03 g/ml. How many full 500 ml bottles does it fill?
finalQuiz.explain: Fill weight is 515 g; 25,000 / 515 = 48.5, so 48 full bottles.

finalQuiz.q: A dilution ladder shows 1 in 200 leaves a film but 1 in 100 cleans well. What dose goes on the label for kitchens?
finalQuiz.explain: The label dose is the weakest rung that cleans well: 1 in 100, which is 50 ml per 5 litre bucket.

finalQuiz.q: Why does this course make glass cleaner without ammonia?
options: A user who later sprays bleach on the same surface could release toxic chloramine gas
finalQuiz.explain: Bleach plus ammonia releases chloramine gases. Leaving ammonia out removes that risk.

finalQuiz.q: Where should the in-use level and contact time for a BKC disinfectant come from?
options: The supplier's technical data sheet for the BKC grade you bought
finalQuiz.explain: The level and contact time depend on the grade and target germs; use the supplier's sheet and record it.

finalQuiz.q: A batch passes pH and flow, but one bottle in ten is under the label fill weight. What is the right decision?
options: Correct the light bottle and check more bottles before release
finalQuiz.explain: No bottle may be under the label amount. Correct and re-check, then record it.

finalQuiz.q: A 20 kg batch costs ₦21,750 and fills 19 bottles. Wholesale price is ₦1,700. What is the profit per batch at wholesale?
Five members each need 6 kg of LABSA a month and bulk buying saves ₦300 per kg. What is the monthly saving per member?
finalQuiz.explain: Each member buys 6 kg and saves ₦300 per kg: 6 x 300 = ₦1,800. The group saves 30 x 300 = ₦9,000 in total.

capstone.title: Production portfolio: three released products
capstone.brief: Produce, test and release three of the six products (one of them must be the laundry detergent or dish liquid, one must be the toilet gel or disinfectant cleaner), pack and label them, and cost one of them to the bottle. Submit an evidence pack that a buyer, NAFDAC officer or cooperative partner could check.
steps: Photograph your production room layout, storage zones and safety station.
Write a percentage formula and a kilogram batch sheet for each of the three products, including the caustic calculation for any LABSA product.
Make each batch with full PPE, recording pH readings, additions and final weight.
Run the five release checks against a written test card for each product and record the decision.
Fill by weight, label each product with directions, warnings and a batch code, and keep a retained sample.
Cost one product fully and set wholesale and retail prices after a three-product market survey.
Write a one-page safety reflection: what went well, any near-miss, and what you changed.
evidence: Three batch sheets with formulas, calculations and pH readings
Three completed test cards with release decisions
Photos of labelled finished products with batch codes
Fill-weight records for ten bottles of one product
